conclusion: Do not adopt the k-removal gate or promote M124. Uniform native phase controls recover15/30 losses, continuous beta inversion4/30, tested k=1/8 gates0/30, unchanged native30/30. Controls14/14 at cutoff in every selected arm. Uniform signs recover identical sets; beta inversion adds one unique recovery, so16/30 is only an oracle union, not a measured selector.
limitations: Single attempt per file/arm,15-second cutoff,selected retrospective sample,not full corpus. No general speedup or absence-of-runtime-regression claim.
Development four all have B=A+20; inversion recoveries all B=A+10. Held-out labels identify cases outside development, not a blinded prospective test.
Probe overhead includes repeated beta computation and active-override scans, including static k=0. Release0 is not timing-equivalent to beta-off.
overridden counts observed decisions while an override is active, not counterfactual changed signs. Agreement does not imply advice caused the choice/conflict.
Arithmetic phase producer skips equality atoms; uniform backend controls cover a broader SAT variable set. Raw input/source audit does not establish equality atoms caused losses.
Same solved set under both forcephase signs suggests native phase evolution/history matters, but does not isolate phase saving from other native mechanisms.
No new assumptions, values, atoms, variable-selection rule, clauses or restart schedule. No production solver policy retained.
